records.name: Gabon
records.summary_text: Gabon demands real caution — and on a surprising positive trajectory: after briefly criminalising same-sex intimacy in 2019, it decriminalised in 2020, and in November 2024 voters ratified a new constitution that rejected calls to criminalise homosexuality. No LGR; social conservatism; but the constitutional debate is now public and the pro-criminalisation side lost.

records.summary_text:
The Republic of the Congo is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal (never criminalised) — but the 2024 official assessment (EUAA COI) documented societal discrimination, police harassment (including bribes extracted under an ambiguous 'acts against nature' provision) and the absence of protection; there is no legal gender recognition, and only a small underground community.
